Learner's Licence Application

State / UT: Rajasthan
Date generated: 16 Nov 2026
Verified: 2026-11-14T00:00:00.000Z

Complete document checklist, ₹200 official statutory fee breakdown, and step-by-step application instructions for Learner Licence across all Indian states.

Required Documents Checklist (5 Items)

Proof of Age (Aadhaar / 10th Marksheet / Birth Certificate)(Mandatory) • Original + 1 self-attested photocopy

Any officially valid document displaying your full date of birth (DD/MM/YYYY).

Proof of Current Residential Address(Mandatory) • Original + 1 photocopy

Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, Electricity Bill, or registered rent agreement in applicant's name.

Form 1 Physical Fitness Self-Declaration(Mandatory) • Filled online during application

Online self-declaration form confirming you have no epilepsy, night blindness, or loss of limbs.

Applicant Signature & Photo Digital Scan(Mandatory) • Scanned file upload (JPEG)

Scanned signature and passport photograph uploaded to the Parivahan Sarathi portal for electronic licence issuance.

Form 1A Medical Fitness Certificate(Conditional) • Original doctor signed copy

Medical certificate signed by a registered MBBS medical practitioner with doctor's registration seal.

Statutory Fees (Official Gazette Rates)

Fee DescriptionTypeAmount (₹)
Learner's Licence Application Processing FeeMandatory₹150
Computerized LL Test FeeMandatory₹50

* Always demand an official computerized government receipt for every rupee paid. Never pay unreceipted cash.

Procedure Steps (Compact Overview)

  1. 1.
    Submit Form 2 on the Sarathi Parivahan Portal[Official Sarathi Portal (parivahan.gov.in)]

    Go to parivahan.gov.in, choose your State, and select 'Apply for Learner Licence'. Fill out your applicant details, address, and select vehicle class (MCWG for geared motorcycle, LMV for car).

  2. 2.
    Upload Required Documents & Photo[Online Portal]

    Upload scanned copies of Proof of Age, Proof of Address, and Form 1 (Self-declaration of physical fitness). If not using Aadhaar e-KYC, upload your signature and passport-size photograph.

  3. 3.
    Pay Government Fee (₹200)[Integrated Bharatkosh / State Payment Gateway]

    Pay the statutory fee of ₹150 for application processing plus ₹50 for computerized test fee via net banking, debit card, or UPI. Download and print payment receipt Form 2.

  4. 4.
    Take the Computerized Learner Test (LL Test)[Online from home (for Aadhaar e-KYC applicants) or at designated RTO Sub-Center]

    Take the 15-question test on traffic signs and road safety. You have 30 seconds per question; score at least 11/15 (60%) to pass. On passing, your digital learner licence (Form 3) is generated instantly.

  5. 5.
    Download & Print Your Digital Learner Licence (Form 3)[Sarathi Parivahan Download Section]

    Immediately upon scoring 11 or higher on the online test, your digital Learner Licence in Form 3 is generated with a verifiable QR code. Download the PDF and keep a physical printout while practicing driving with an instructor.

Step-by-Step Procedure

Follow these sequential steps from online registration to final counter collection.

1

Submit Form 2 on the Sarathi Parivahan Portal

Official Sarathi Portal (parivahan.gov.in)15 minutes

Go to parivahan.gov.in, choose your State, and select 'Apply for Learner Licence'. Fill out your applicant details, address, and select vehicle class (MCWG for geared motorcycle, LMV for car).

Aadhaar e-KYC Tip

If your mobile number is linked to Aadhaar, choose 'Applicant with Aadhaar' for paperless online verification without an in-person RTO visit for document submission.
Open Sarathi Parivahan Application Portal
2

Upload Required Documents & Photo

Online Portal10 minutes

Upload scanned copies of Proof of Age, Proof of Address, and Form 1 (Self-declaration of physical fitness). If not using Aadhaar e-KYC, upload your signature and passport-size photograph.

3

Pay Government Fee (₹200)

Integrated Bharatkosh / State Payment Gateway5 minutes

Pay the statutory fee of ₹150 for application processing plus ₹50 for computerized test fee via net banking, debit card, or UPI. Download and print payment receipt Form 2.

Keep Payment Receipt Safe

Print the e-receipt immediately. The transaction reference number is required if payment status enters 'Pending'.
4

Take the Computerized Learner Test (LL Test)

Online from home (for Aadhaar e-KYC applicants) or at designated RTO Sub-Center20 minutes

Take the 15-question test on traffic signs and road safety. You have 30 seconds per question; score at least 11/15 (60%) to pass. On passing, your digital learner licence (Form 3) is generated instantly.

5

Download & Print Your Digital Learner Licence (Form 3)

Sarathi Parivahan Download Section5 minutes

Immediately upon scoring 11 or higher on the online test, your digital Learner Licence in Form 3 is generated with a verifiable QR code. Download the PDF and keep a physical printout while practicing driving with an instructor.

Keep QR Code Legible

Traffic police and licensing authorities verify learner licences by scanning the QR code directly using their handheld mParivahan terminals.

What to Do After Submission: Status Tracking & Collection

Once you submit your application and biometric verification is complete:

  • Keep the Acknowledgement Slip: Safely note your Application Number or SMS reference to track status on the official portal.
  • Delivery via Speed Post: Physical cards or renewed booklets are dispatched to your registered address via India Post Speed Post with tracking.
  • Digital Download (DigiLocker / mParivahan): Legally valid digital documents become available on DigiLocker immediately upon counter approval under IT Act Rule 9A.

Why Applications Get Rejected

Review these top 1 counter rejection triggers before visiting the office.

Common Mistakes

Name or Date of Birth Mismatch on Aadhaar

Rejection Risk #1

If the name on your 10th marksheet or birth certificate does not match the name returned by Aadhaar e-KYC, the application is halted.

How to avoid: Update your Aadhaar details first at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra, or apply via non-Aadhaar mode with physical document scrutiny at the RTO.

Frequently Asked Questions

Common citizen doubts answered according to official Ministry circulars.

4 Answers

A Learner's Licence is valid for exactly 6 months (180 days) from the date of issue across all states and Union Territories.

No. You must be accompanied by someone who holds a valid permanent driving licence for that vehicle. Also, your vehicle must display red 'L' plates on front and back.

The computerized learner test consists of 15 multiple-choice questions covering Indian road signs, traffic signals, and fundamental driving regulations. You must answer at least 11 questions correctly (60% score) within the allotted 30 seconds per question to pass.

You can apply for a permanent driving licence after 30 days from your Learner Licence issue date. You must apply within 180 days (6 months) before the learner licence expires.

Before You Leave Home

Verify these 5 essential physical items before walking out your door in Rajasthan.

Check #1

All Original Documents

Carry physical originals of all proof papers (Aadhaar, proof of address, birth date proof) for live verification at the counter for Learner's Licence Application.

Check #2

2 Sets of Self-Attested Photocopies

Black-and-white photocopies signed with your signature and today's date in blue or black ink across the blank margin.

Check #3

Passport Photographs

2 to 4 recent passport photos (35mm x 45mm, plain white background, front-facing without tinted glasses).

Check #4

Accepted Payment Mode

UPI app or active debit card for statutory portal fees, plus ₹200–₹500 exact cash change if counter fees apply.

Check #5

Appointment Slip & SMS

Physical printout of your appointment booking acknowledgment receipt & application reference number (ARN).
